note: Spellcasting as a shop service (core/game/game_casting.gd, specified in docs/SHOP_SERVICES.md, checked by tools/check_data.gd). A shop with `services` rows of kind `cast` casts one of the spells of data/spells/spells.json FOR the heir, for gold: it is a purchase, so the heir's own mana is not spent and the spell never needs to be known. Only the party-shaped utility spells are for sale (`healing`: mass_heal; `cleansing`: cleanse; `blessing`: ward, haste, rejuvenation), because a shop acts on the heir and the party, not on foes. Outside a fight a healing spell mends the heir and the companions at once by the spell's own `pct_max_hp`, a cleansing spell cures every sickness the heir has (and mends its own small share), no time passes and no dice are drawn; a blessing is carried into the NEXT fight and applied to the heir and every companion when it begins (the spell's own statuses, at the spell's own turns), and then lapses: one at a time (a second replaces it), at most `fights` fights, at most `years` years, and it ends with the heir. A row's `caster_level` strengthens the spell by `level_step` for each level above 1 and raises the price by `price_step` for each; the price is the spell's own `mp` times `mp_gold` times that, then the shop's prices (GameItems.price_mult). A cast has a cooldown of a day by default (`daily`): the same spell at the same shop is not cast twice in one day of the world clock (the year and the GameDay day number), so a shop is not a free full heal every fight. Nothing is random; the blessing and the day marks are saved only when set.

text.healed: {name} pays {price} gold at {shop}: the party is mended ({what}).
text.blessed: {name} pays {price} gold at {shop}: {spell} is laid on the party for the next fight.
text.no_need: {name} and the party need no mending.
text.cooldown: {shop} has cast {spell} for you today; it will cast it again tomorrow.
text.same: {spell} is already laid on the party.
